content: Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid medication that mimics a natural hormone produced by the adrenal glands. It is prescribed to replace this hormone when the body does not produce enough of it. This medication is effective in reducing inflammation, which includes symptoms such as swelling, heat, redness, and pain. It is commonly used to treat conditions such as certain types of arthritis, disorders affecting the skin, blood, kidneys, eyes, thyroid, and intestines (e.g., colitis), severe allergies, and asthma. Additionally, dexamethasone is used in the treatment of certain cancers. If you have questions about other potential uses of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Dexamethasone is available in tablet form or as an oral solution. Your doctor will provide a specific dosing schedule tailored to your condition. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Do not stop taking dexamethasone without consulting your doctor, as abrupt discontinuation can lead to withdrawal symptoms such as loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, drowsiness, confusion, headache, fever, joint and muscle pain, peeling skin, and weight loss. If you have been on high doses for an extended period, your doctor will likely reduce your dose gradually to allow your body to adjust. Be vigilant for withdrawal symptoms during the tapering process or after stopping the medication, even if you switch to an inhaled form. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately, as you may need to temporarily increase your dose or restart the medication. Before starting dexamethasone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to dexamethasone, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some foods and medications), or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), arthritis medications, aspirin, cyclosporine, digoxin, diuretics, ephedrine, estrogen, ketoconazole, oral contraceptives, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampin, theophylline, and vitamins. If you have a fungal infection (other than a skin infection), consult your doctor before taking dexamethasone. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking dexamethasone, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking dexamethasone. If you have a history of ulcers or are taking high doses of aspirin or arthritis medications, limit your alcohol consumption, as dexamethasone increases the risk of stomach and intestinal irritation, which can lead to ulcers. Your doctor may recommend dietary modifications while you are taking dexamethasone, such as a low-sodium, low-salt, potassium-rich, or high-protein diet. Follow these instructions carefully. To minimize stomach upset, take dexamethasone with food or milk. If you miss a dose of dexamethasone, ask your doctor for specific instructions on what to do. Write these instructions down for future reference. If you take the medication once daily, take the missed dose as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Dexamethasone may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, stomach irritation, vomiting, headache, dizziness, insomnia, restlessness, depression, anxiety, acne, increased hair growth, easy bruising, and irregular or absent menstrual periods. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include skin rash, swelling of the face, lower legs, or ankles, vision problems, prolonged infections or colds, muscle weakness, and black or tarry stools. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store dexamethasone in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular monitoring is necessary to assess your response to dexamethasone. This is particularly important for children, as the medication can slow bone growth. If your condition worsens, notify your doctor, as your dosage may need adjustment. Carry an identification card indicating that you may require additional doses of dexamethasone during periods of stress, such as injuries, infections, or severe asthma attacks. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how to obtain this card, and include your name, medical conditions, medications, dosages, and your doctor's contact information on it. Dexamethasone can increase your susceptibility to infections. If you are exposed to chickenpox, measles, or tuberculosis while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid vaccinations, immunizations, or skin tests unless your doctor approves. Report any injuries or signs of infection, such as fever, sore throat, pain during urination, or muscle aches, to your doctor. Your doctor may instruct you to monitor your weight daily and report any unusual weight gain. If you have diabetes, dexamethasone may raise your blood sugar levels. Test your blood or urine more frequently and notify your doctor if your blood sugar is elevated or if sugar is present in your urine, as your diabetes medication or diet may need adjustment. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Dexamethasone is sold under various brand names, including Decadron®, Decadron® 5-12 Pak®, Decadron® Phosphate, Decaject®, Decaject-LA®, Dexamethasone Intensol®, Dexone LA®, Dexpak® Taperpak®, Solurex LA®, and Solurex®.
